judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse unconditionally (in both the credential-sharing and the default path) replaces a missing refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" before the parsed object is persisted as the credential key. On the default (non-sync) path for apps whose refresh responses legitimately omit refresh_token (e.g. some providers rotate only access tokens), the credential key is silently overwritten with a bogus refresh_token; the next refresh attempt sends the literal string 'refresh_token' to the provider and fails permanently — a behavior change to unrelated flows not required by the credential-sync feature.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, after a successful parse the code unconditionally sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when it is missing. This happens regardless of whether the credential-sharing path or the default schema path is used. Call sites then use the parsed result to build/persist updated credentials (e.g. Office365: `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };`), so a provider response that omits `refresh_token` can lead to the stored refresh token being overwritten with the literal string, breaking future refreshes.
